youtube.title: Why does your slipper sole have a zigzag? 🩴 #Shorts #science #facts #didyouknow
youtube.description:
A thin film of water between smooth rubber and a floor works like a lubricant, and the shoe can float on it. The grooves and zigzag channels in a sole (called tread) act as drains: when you step, water is pushed out through the channels so the rubber ridges touch the floor and grip. Tread with sharp edges also bites into the film, which is why worn-flat soles are so slippery on wet tiles.
